title: Architecture of the CPU
starter: The same laptop can run a game, then a word processor, then a browser, with no hardware changed. What makes that possible?
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: John von Neumann
facts: A Hungarian-American mathematician and computer scientist.
In 1945 he described a design for a computer that stores programs in memory.
Nearly all modern computers still follow his ideas.
stations.challenge: Who was John von Neumann, and why is he important to computing?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A Hungarian-American mathematician and computer scientist.
Also credit: In 1945 he described a design for a computer that stores programs in memory.

questions.q: What is John von Neumann best known for in computing?
questions.a: Describing a computer design where programs are stored in memory

questions.q: When did von Neumann describe his architecture?

stations.name: The stored-program concept
facts: Instructions and data are both stored in the same main memory.
The CPU fetches instructions and data from memory, one at a time.
Loading a different program means the same computer can do a different job.
stations.challenge: Explain how data and instructions are stored in von Neumann architecture.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Instructions and data are both stored in the same main memory.
Also credit: The CPU fetches instructions and data from memory, one at a time.

questions.q: In von Neumann architecture, where are instructions stored?
questions.a: In main memory, together with the data

questions.q: Why is the stored-program idea so useful?
questions.a: The same computer can run different programs just by loading them into memory

stations.name: Program counter and accumulator
facts: Program counter (PC): holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched.
It increments during each fetch-decode-execute cycle.
Accumulator (ACC): holds the results of calculations done by the ALU.
stations.challenge: Explain the purpose of the program counter and how its value changes.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Program counter (PC): holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched.
Also credit: It increments during each fetch-decode-execute cycle.

questions.q: What does the program counter hold?
questions.a: The address of the next instruction

questions.q: Which register holds the results of calculations?

stations.name: MAR and MDR
facts: MAR (memory address register): holds the address of the data or instruction to be fetched or stored.
MDR (memory data register): holds the data or instruction fetched from memory, or to be written to it.
They work as a pair to move data between the CPU and RAM.
stations.challenge: Describe the purpose of the memory data register.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: MAR (memory address register): holds the address of the data or instruction to be fetched or stored.
Also credit: MDR (memory data register): holds the data or instruction fetched from memory, or to be written to it.

questions.q: Which register holds the address of data to be fetched from memory?

questions.a: Data or an instruction fetched from memory, or waiting to be written to memory

stations.name: Other architectures
facts: Harvard architecture stores instructions and data in separate memories, with separate buses.
It lets an instruction and data be fetched at the same time.
It's used in many embedded systems and microcontrollers.
stations.challenge: What other architectures exist, and where are they used?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Harvard architecture stores instructions and data in separate memories, with separate buses.
Also credit: It lets an instruction and data be fetched at the same time.

questions.q: What is the main difference in Harvard architecture?
questions.a: Instructions and data are held in separate memories

questions.q: Where is Harvard architecture commonly used?

stations.name: Keywords
facts: Every programming language has keywords: reserved words with a special meaning.
Python keywords include if, else, while, for, def, return, True and False.
You can't use a keyword as a variable name.
stations.challenge: Find three Python keywords and write what each one does.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Every programming language has keywords: reserved words with a special meaning.
Also credit: Python keywords include if, else, while, for, def, return, True and False.

questions.q: Which of these is a Python keyword?
Why can't you call a variable 'if'?
questions.a: It's a keyword with a special meaning in the language

final.name: Final challenge: name that part

questions.q: Match each component or register to its definition.
questions.a: Program counter → Stores the address of the next instruction; increments each cycle; Control unit → Decodes instructions and sends control signals; MAR → Stores the address of the data to be fetched or stored; ALU → Performs mathematical calculations and logical operations; MDR → Stores data fetched from, or to be written to, memory; Accumulator → Stores the results of calculations; Cache → Fast memory for frequently used instructions and data

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
